prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a redesigned ORVASK 10-capacity expedition outfit concept sheet. This replaces the previous plain-coat/oversized shoulder apparatus approach with an INTEGRATED SEALED SURVIVAL EXPLORER SUIT.
INPUT ROLES: Input1 approved game's hero, use adult lean proportions and VERY broad muted chunky pixel clusters as authoritative art style. Its old hat is expressly NOT locked for this new outfit. Inputs2,3,4 are user supplied COSTUME DESIGN references only, NOT rendering style. Input3's work jacket and enclosed visor helmet are the main human/practical clothing influence, input4's long layered coat and integrated breathing equipment the secondary silhouette influence, input2 contributes sealed collar and chest life-support fittings. Interpret into a unique original costume; don't reproduce logos, insignia, specific gear arrangement or photoreal detail.
DESIGN: A veteran explorer of poisoned upper tower districts. Worn rounded low-profile slate/gray-green enclosed industrial helmet with short brow and one broad smoky dark visor, tiny rectangular warm lamp mounted off-center. Face enclosed, no original earflap hat. Thick sealed fabric collar with a small rust-red scarf tab tucked under it, not a large draped scarf. A single broad breathing hose comes from helmet jaw/side down to a compact bone-gray/orange filter unit on upper chest; it must connect clearly and not loop across shooting hands. Grey-olive thick cloth long work coat with wide collar, split tails ending near knees, rolled/reinforced sleeve cuffs, one muted ochre upper-arm panel, dark harness across torso. Slight asymmetry from a compact chest instrument, one broad hip satchel, side canister and reinforced knee, not ornate pauldrons. Backpack is compact integrated life-support: two broad enclosed vertical air/filter modules under one worn fabric hood, one circular side connector and short attached hose, folded blanket low; hugs the torso, head unobstructed. Work gloves and heavy brown boots. Wear conveyed through broad color patches and one or two repaired fabric shapes. Human survival suit, not a cyborg/robot, no extra limbs, no exposed decorative gears, giant shoulder arch, wings or halo. Silhouette should be distinctive through helmet, sealed collar, hose and layered coat, not arbitrary added panels.
SHEET: wide 3:2 neutral flat medium slate background, two full body equal-height figures, left front three-quarter facing right, right rear three-quarter facing left to clearly show back. Consistent exact outfit and asymmetry on both views. Relaxed neutral standing empty hands slightly clear of hips, NO gun; enough future arm/gun clearance. Feet same baseline. Generous borders. No text or decorative UI.
PIXEL STYLE IS CRITICAL: input1's quiet broad pixel masses; approximately 50-60 logical pixels wide x100-110 high per figure, enlarged crisp nearest neighbor appearance. Strong LARGE square stair steps, flat big fabric shapes, only2-3 grouped values per material, restrained selective edges. Keep a clear clean silhouette. No tiny bolts, individual hose rib lines, loose thin cables, dense seams, shiny outlines, texture grain, dithering, photorealism, painting, blurred edges or smoothly shaded concept illustration. Visor is one dark color mass plus ONE muted reflection block, not glowing eyes. Technical details must be simplified into large readable symbols/shapes. Use restrained slate/olive, warm gray, brown, small ochre and rust red accents; no white shine or saturated neon. This is a game pixel costume concept, not a realistic sci-fi concept rendered then pixel filtered.
status: concept only, not integrated; user preference pending
review: Sealed visor helmet, hose, chest filter and twin rear life-support modules provide intended integrated survival silhouette. Hat deliberately replaced in this outfit under latest reference direction. Gloves, adult proportions and long coat retained. More surface detail than minimal battle actor; simplify hose ribs/seams and verify front-rear equipment correspondence before sprite production. No runtime QA.
